events.title: Sun Enterprise 10000 released
events.summary: Sun Microsystems shipped the Enterprise 10000 ("Starfire") in 1996 — a massively scalable [Unix] server for datacenter workloads.
events.about: The E10K packed dozens of UltraSPARC CPUs in a single cabinet — banks, telcos, and dot-coms ran Oracle, SAP, and custom Java services on it. For backend developers, Starfire represented the high end of the Solaris ecosystem before Linux on commodity [x86] took over datacenters. Hot-swappable boards and partitioning foreshadowed cloud instance sizing.

narrative.whyChosen: The Enterprise 10000 was Sun's flagship datacenter [Unix] server of the dot-com era.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed how [Unix] servers scaled vertically before horizontal Linux clusters dominated.
narrative.problemSolved: Enterprises needed single-system image [Unix] servers with 64+ processors for massive databases and transaction processing.

events.title: Richard Stallman: "free as in speech, not beer"
events.quoteText: Think of 'free' as in 'free speech,' not as in 'free beer.'
events.summary: Richard Stallman clarifies [free software] as freedom to use and modify code — not zero price.
events.about: The phrase appears in GNU philosophy writing and talks as Stallman fought the confusion between gratis downloads and user freedom. It still surfaces in every LGPL vs [MIT] license thread.

narrative.whyChosen: Stallman's most effective one-liner for a politically loaded term.
narrative.whyImportant: It separated libre from gratis in open-source debates for decades.
narrative.problemSolved: Businesses and users conflated '[free software]' with unpaid products.
